subtopicTitle: Simple harmonic motion — definition, restoring force F = -kx

cards.front: What is the fundamental defining characteristic of Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)?
cards.back: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM) is a type of periodic motion where the restoring force acting on the oscillating object is directly proportional to its displacement from the equilibrium position and always acts in the opposite direction to the displacement.

cards.front: State the mathematical expression for the restoring force in a system undergoing Simple Harmonic Motion, also known as Hooke's Law.
cards.back: The restoring force $F$ in SHM is given by Hooke's Law: $$F = -kx$$

cards.front: In the equation $F = -kx$, what do $F$, $k$, and $x$ represent, including their standard SI units?
cards.back:
• $F$: Restoring force (in Newtons, N)
  • $k$: Spring constant or force constant (in Newtons per meter, N/m)
  • $x$: Displacement from the equilibrium position (in meters, m)

cards.front: Explain the physical significance of the negative sign in the restoring force equation $F = -kx$.
cards.back: The negative sign indicates that the restoring force $F$ always acts in the opposite direction to the displacement $x$. If the object is displaced to the right ($x > 0$), the force pulls it left ($F < 0$). If displaced to the left ($x < 0$), the force pushes it right ($F > 0$). This force always tries to return the object to its equilibrium position.

cards.front: What are the two essential conditions a system must satisfy for its motion to be classified as Simple Harmonic Motion?
cards.back:
1. There must be a restoring force that is directly proportional to the displacement from the equilibrium position.
2. This restoring force must always act towards the equilibrium position (opposite to the direction of displacement).

cards.front: A mass attached to a spring with a spring constant $k = 120 \text{ N/m}$ is stretched $20 \text{ cm}$ from its equilibrium position. Calculate the magnitude and direction of the restoring force.
cards.back:
Given: $k = 120 \text{ N/m}$, $x = 20 \text{ cm} = 0.20 \text{ m}$.
Using Hooke's Law, $F = -kx$.
$F = -(120 \text{ N/m})(0.20 \text{ m})$
$F = -24 \text{ N}$.
The magnitude of the restoring force is $24 \text{ N}$. The negative sign indicates it acts in the direction opposite to the displacement (i.e., towards the equilibrium position).

cards.front: How does the 'equilibrium position' relate to the restoring force in Simple Harmonic Motion?
cards.back: The equilibrium position is the specific point where the net force acting on the oscillating object is zero. In SHM, the restoring force $F = -kx$ becomes zero precisely when $x = 0$, which defines the equilibrium position. The restoring force always acts to bring the object back to this zero-force, equilibrium point.
